title: BalancerPoolerV2 never sweeps dispatcher-held USDS into sUSDS — orphaned USDS earns no DSR yield for NFT holders
description: Story-025 makes USDS the mint currency and wraps to sUSDS in _dispatch. The wrap uses the `amount` parameter passed from NFTMinterV2 (the per-mint `actualReceived`) rather than the dispatcher's full USDS balance: `IERC4626(_sUSDS).deposit(amount, address(this))`. `pool(minBPT)` later pools only the current sUSDS balance; it never looks at the dispatcher's USDS balance. As a consequence, any USDS that arrives on BalancerPoolerV2 outside the exact `_executeMint -> dispatch(amount)` path is never wrapped to sUSDS and never ends up in Balancer as BPT. Sources of orphaned USDS include: (a) accidental or griefing donations sent directly to the dispatcher (the address is public once registered), (b) a USDS balance left behind by a failed downstream integration, (c) a future path that lands USDS on this dispatcher without going through NFTMinterV2. Unlike sUSDS, USDS itself is non-yield-bearing — every block of delay represents foregone DSR yield to NFT holders.
impact: Any USDS landing on BalancerPoolerV2 outside the normal mint path becomes dead weight: it accrues zero DSR yield and is excluded from the BPT pool that backs NFT holders. Recoverable only via owner `rescueERC20`, which routes value to a single owner-chosen recipient rather than back into the BPT that credits all NFT holders. Non-attacker-driven but a structural yield-leakage surface introduced by the story-026 decoupled wrap-then-pool design.
attack_path: Anyone transfers X USDS directly to the BalancerPoolerV2 address (0 cost to grief, could also be accidental).
Subsequent mints call _dispatch(minter, amount, ...) where `amount` is only the new mint's FOT-adjusted USDS.
_dispatch's IERC4626.deposit wraps only that `amount`, leaving X USDS idle on the dispatcher.
pool(minBPT) later reads only sUSDS balance; X USDS never reaches Balancer.
X USDS accrues 0 DSR yield until owner manually rescueERC20's it (and rescueERC20 routes to a single address, not back to NFT holders).
recommendation: In _dispatch, wrap the dispatcher's full USDS balance rather than only the `amount` argument: `uint256 toWrap = IERC20(_primeToken).balanceOf(address(this)); IERC20(_primeToken).forceApprove(_sUSDS, toWrap); IERC4626(_sUSDS).deposit(toWrap, address(this));`. This guarantees any stray USDS is swept into sUSDS on every mint. Alternatively, add a permissionless `sweepUSDS()` function — no privileges needed because no value leaves the dispatcher.
dedupNote: Unique. Yield-leakage surface created by story-025/026 decoupled wrap-then-pool design (USDS lands on dispatcher; only the per-mint `amount` is wrapped to sUSDS). Round-02 L-04 / round-03 L-04 cover missing rescueERC20 on Gather/Burner dispatchers — different contracts, and rescueERC20 doesn't address the structural sweep issue. Not covered by knownIssues.
sanitizeNote: In V2 focus area (stories 025+026 BalancerPoolerV2 wrap-then-pool design). Trigger is permissionless donation/grief, NOT owner-driven — owner's role (rescueERC20) is the inadequate mitigation, not the attack vector. No match against project knownIssues; the FOT balance-before/after known-issue pattern is unrelated (this is about USDS arriving outside the dispatch path, not FOT mid-transfer).
classifyNote: C4 regular-audit Low/QA — borderline considered against Medium and rejected. Why not Medium: (1) Principal is not at risk — owner can recover via rescueERC20. Only foregone DSR yield is at stake, capped at donation_amount * idle_duration * DSR_rate (single-digit % annualized). (2) Griefing is economically self-defeating: the griefer must forfeit their own yield-bearing capacity on the same USDS to deny the protocol a proportional slice of yield — asymmetric against the attacker, not the protocol. There is no rational at-scale grief. (3) The 'lost yield is non-trivial' bar isn't met: yield accrues only on amounts deliberately and voluntarily donated by external actors; the protocol's own expected USDS flows always go through _executeMint -> dispatch(amount) and ARE wrapped. No protocol-originated path strands USDS. (4) C4 'loss of yield' guidance: matured yield ~= capital, but unmatured/in-motion yield is capped at Medium AND dust amounts go to QA. Here the leaked yield isn't even on protocol capital — it's on attacker-supplied capital. (5) C4 explicitly downgrades 'centralization mitigations available' style issues; rescueERC20 exists. Closer to a sweep-pattern code-quality / spec issue than a value-leak finding. Confirm Low. Strong recommendation regardless because the fix (sweep full balance in _dispatch, or add permissionless sweepUSDS()) is ~2 lines and removes the surface entirely.
validityNote: Present-day reachable code path: anyone can transfer USDS to the public dispatcher address today and _dispatch's IERC4626.deposit(amount, ...) will not sweep it. No future-code or future-hook assumption required. Root cause is fully in-scope (BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch / pool). Not a user-mistake / admin-mistake / FOT / approve-race pattern. Strongest of the five Lows on validity grounds — keep as a standalone L-entry.
